clue.text: A river skirts Crosby, a town in England

indicators.note: to skirt something is to run along its edges, so the first words go around the singer's name

blocks.note: taken as written
Bing Crosby, the American crooner
the Don, a river in Yorkshire and in Russia

explanation.surface: A river winds past the edge of Crosby, a town on Merseyside.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosby looks like the Merseyside town, but it is the singer Bing. Abingdon is a market town on the Thames in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Abingdon is a historic market town in Oxfordshire, so it is an example of an English town.

clue.text: A couple of fellows skate and row

definitions.note: a row in the sense of a noisy quarrel

blocks.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for fellow; two of them
a skate is a kind of ray, a flat fish

explanation.surface: Two men go ice-skating and then out in a rowing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Skate and row both look like verbs of exercise; one is a fish and the other a quarrel, rhyming with 'cow'.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public fight or brawl, the noisy disturbance meant by a row.

clue.text: It's incongruous that one club supports another

indicators.note: in a down entry what supports something sits underneath it, so the one-and-club letters come below

blocks.note: an iron is a golf club, the other club here
Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: It seems odd that one golf club should hold up another one.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the letters for 'one club' sit below and so support the golf club above them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ironic is strikingly at odds with what was expected, which is what incongruous describes.

clue.text: A shufti round site of air traffic control centre

definitions.text: site of air traffic control centre

blocks.note: first meaning: a quick look around

blocks.clueFragment: site of air traffic control centre
blocks.note: second meaning: the Newfoundland town whose centre handles North Atlantic flights

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quick look around an air traffic control building.
explanation.walkthrough: Shufti is British slang, from army Arabic, for a quick look. Gander in Newfoundland hosts the oceanic control centre for transatlantic air traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A gander is slang for a glance, and Gander is the Canadian town whose control centre guides flights crossing the Atlantic.

clue.text: Public beneficiary receives a broadcast

definitions.note: broadcast as an adverb: by radio or television

indicators.note: the beneficiary takes in the letter, so it is placed inside that word

blocks.note: overt means open, done in public
an heir benefits from a will
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who gains from public money is handed a broadcasting slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Programmes sent over the air are transmitted by radio waves, which is what broadcast means here.

clue.text: Son strode out when out of his skull

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
paced means walked with long steps

explanation.surface: A young man marched off while he was badly drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced is slang for dazed or high, the drugged state also called being out of one's skull.

clue.text: Plain language written about border flower

indicators.note: language written around something wraps it, so the border word goes inside

blocks.note: prose is ordinary language without metre
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Simple wording is used to describe a flower bed's edging plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring wildflower, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Danish king receives ancient request for wood

indicators.note: the king takes the request into himself, so it sits inside his name

blocks.note: Cnut (Canute), the Danish king of England
hest is an archaic word for a command or request, as in behest

explanation.surface: A Danish king is given an old petition asking for timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Cnut is the older spelling of King Canute, who ruled England, Denmark and Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnut is the timber of the chestnut tree, so it names a kind of wood.

clue.text: Water soaking away from bedraggled gardenia

indicators.note: a bedraggled flower is knocked out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Rain runs off a dishevelled gardenia in a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainage is the process of water running off or seeping away through soil or pipes.

clue.text: Sovereign introduced to metalworker! That's a fluke!

indicators.note: the coin is put into the worker's name, so it goes inside

blocks.note: a founder casts metal in a foundry
a sovereign is a pound coin, and L stands for pound

explanation.surface: A gold coin turns up at the foundry by sheer luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Fluke looks like a lucky chance, but it is also the name of a flatfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluke and flounder are both names for flatfish, so one fish stands for the other.

clue.text: Spooks beset people returning from place of entertainment

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so the spooks enclose the people
going back means the word for people is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: spooks are spies; the CIA is the US spy agency
men, read backwards

explanation.surface: Spies ambush people on their way home from a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema is a building where films are shown, a place people go to be entertained.

clue.text: Drink tisane brewed by Lawrence

indicators.note: brewing a drink mixes its ingredients, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of tisane rearranged
T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Lawrence makes himself a pot of herbal tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur, a kind of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Native of seaside resort with no good hotel

indicators.note: having none of something means those letters are taken out of the resort's name

blocks.note: Brighton, the resort on the Sussex coast
G is the abbreviation for good
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A local from a seaside town can't find a decent hotel there.
explanation.definitionFit: A Briton is a person born in Britain, a native of the country.

clue.text: Statesman embraces one and all on the island. That's sweet

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within one's arms, so the statesman's letters go around

blocks.note: the Prime Minister, a statesman
each means every one, all taken singly
Elba, Napoleon's island of exile

explanation.surface: A politician hugs everyone on holiday on an island, which is a lovely gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' puts the first part above the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Peach melba is a dessert of peaches, ice cream and raspberry sauce, and sweet is the British word for a dessert course.

clue.text: City in America canonised in Russia

blocks.note: first meaning: a city in Virginia
second meaning: the Russian city becomes a saint when it is given its full name

explanation.surface: An American city shares its name with a holy Russian one.
explanation.walkthrough: The Russian city is St Petersburg, so its name made a saint (canonised) is the name without the St.
explanation.definitionFit: Petersburg is a city in Virginia, and adding Saint gives the Russian former capital.

clue.text: Kitchen staff gather in Israel

indicators.note: the gathering word is placed inside the name for Israel

blocks.note: Sion, a variant spelling of Zion, the land of Israel
to cull is to pick or gather

explanation.surface: Kitchen workers assemble somewhere in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullion was a lowly servant doing the rough work in a kitchen, such as washing pots.

clue.text: Rodent roomed with us unfortunately

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so the letters fall into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rodent was our unwelcome lodger.
explanation.definitionFit: The dormouse is a small hibernating rodent, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Iron Age re-settlement looking initially to be from a certain area

indicators.note: settling something again puts it down in a new arrangement
initially points to the first letter of looking

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of looking

explanation.surface: An archaeologist eyes a resettled Iron Age community as local to one district.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional means belonging to or characteristic of a particular region or district.

clue.text: Companion embraces sweetheart with desire - not as it's reported

indicators.note: an embrace holds someone inside one's arms, so the companion's letters go around

blocks.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
love is a term for a sweetheart
an itch is a craving

explanation.surface: A companion hugs a lover with longing, though not, apparently, as the gossip has it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sound: 'not', as spoken, is a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove hitch is a simple knot used to fasten a rope around a post, and knot sounds exactly like not.

clue.text: Tinker takes one kind of food

blocks.note: tinker and scamp both mean a mischievous child
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A travelling mender helps himself to a single dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Tinker looks like the pot-mender, but in Britain it is also a word for a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustine tails, usually fried in breadcrumbs, a popular seafood dish.

clue.text: Apron for local tucking into tart

indicators.note: something tucking into a dish goes inside it

blocks.note: a tart is a pie
a local is one's neighbourhood pub, an inn

explanation.surface: A pub regular puts on a bib to eat a tart.
explanation.walkthrough: Tucking into looks like eating, but it means going inside. The local is British for the nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnie is an informal British word for a pinafore, a sleeveless apron.

clue.text: Brown coal left off fire

indicators.note: the letter for left comes off the coal, removed from it

blocks.note: lignite is soft brown coal
L for left

explanation.surface: Lignite is left out of the fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire something is to set it alight, which is what ignite means.

clue.text: It is quite clear the monkey is wearing a hat

indicators.note: the monkey wears the hat, so the hat's letters go around it

blocks.note: lid is slang for a hat
a monkey is a mischievous child, an imp

explanation.surface: Plainly, the zoo monkey has a hat on.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid water is perfectly transparent, completely clear.

clue.text: Bob's making fun of needlework

blocks.note: a bob is an old British shilling, abbreviated s
mocking means ridiculing

explanation.surface: Bob is teasing someone about their embroidery.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob looks like a man's name, but it is slang for a shilling, the old coin written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Smocking is decorative embroidery that gathers fabric into tight pleats, a kind of needlework.

clue.text: Reptilian soldier turned to university articles

definitions.note: used as a noun: a reptile

indicators.note: turned round means the soldier's letters are read backwards

blocks.note: GI is an American soldier
U for university
two articles, an and a

explanation.surface: A cold-blooded soldier went off to college to write papers.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical lizard, and so is a reptile.

clue.text: Writer of note from Fair Isle

blocks.note: clement weather is fair and mild
I is an abbreviation for isle

explanation.surface: A famous author comes from Fair Isle in the Shetlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle looks like the Shetland island, but the two words are separate. A writer of notes is a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Muzio Clementi was an Italian composer of piano music, someone who wrote music.

clue.text: The Parisian follows requirement for a sewer

definitions.note: the thing used by someone who sews

indicators.note: coming after means the French word is placed behind the requirement

blocks.note: a need is a requirement
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's needs come after what a drain requires.
explanation.walkthrough: Sewer suggests a drain, but here it is someone who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A needle is the pointed tool a person sewing uses to pull thread through cloth.

clue.text: The railway in an army camp on an island

definitions.note: adjective: belonging to the island of Bali

indicators.note: the railway is placed inside the word for camp

blocks.note: a base is a military camp
a railway line

explanation.surface: A railway runs through a military camp on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Balinese describes people or things from Bali, the Indonesian island.
